note: All data cross-checked against current EPA-registered product labels (CDMS/Greenbook/EPA PPLS) and University of Minnesota Extension, Penn State Extension, Michigan State University Extension, and Crop Protection Network sources as of June 2026. Pesticide rates, PHIs, and application limits vary by state and change between label updates, so this file should be re-verified against the current, state-specific product label before being used to generate real-world recommendations. The LLM must not suggest any medication, dosage, or timing not listed here.

rust.description: Southern corn rust (Puccinia polysora) appears as small, circular to oval pustules on the upper leaf surface. Pustules are orange-tan to cinnamon-brown. Common in warm, humid seasons.
cultural_controls: Plant rust-resistant hybrids where available
Scout fields regularly from tasseling through dough stage
Monitor regional disease forecasts (e.g., USDA risk maps)

medications.timing: Apply at first sign of rust pustules or when regional forecasts indicate elevated risk. Most effective applied before or very early in the epidemic.
medications.notes: In field corn, do not make more than 2 sequential applications per year before rotating to a non-Group 11 fungicide. Maximum seasonal rate across all uses (foliar + in-furrow) is 72 fl oz/acre/year (1.18 lb ai pyraclostrobin).
medications.research_source: University of Minnesota Extension / Crop Protection Network / EPA product label
medications.severity_threshold: Economic threshold generally reached when >5% of leaf area shows pustules before or at tasseling on susceptible hybrids

medications.timing: Apply at first sign of disease. Premix provides dual mode of action, reducing resistance risk.
medications.notes: Do not apply within 30 days of harvest for forage, grain, or stover. Label allows 2 applications at the 14 fl oz rate or 3 at the 10.5 fl oz rate per year.
medications.research_source: Crop Protection Network — Fungicide Efficacy for Control of Corn Foliar Diseases / EPA product label
medications.severity_threshold: Same as single-mode products; premix preferred when disease pressure is high

gray_leaf.description: Gray leaf spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis) produces rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions bounded by leaf veins. Severe infections can cause premature leaf death and significant yield loss.
cultural_controls: Rotate away from corn at least one year to reduce inoculum
Manage infected crop residue through tillage or promotion of residue breakdown
Plant resistant or tolerant hybrids — the most cost-effective control
Improve field drainage and airflow where possible

medications.dosage_rate: 3–12 fl oz/acre (3–4 fl oz/acre for early-season V3–V7 suppression; 6–12 fl oz/acre at VT–R3)
medications.timing: Apply at or just before tasseling (VT–R1) when scouting shows disease present on the ear leaf or above under susceptible hybrid conditions.
medications.notes: No more than 2 sequential applications before shifting to a fungicide with a different mode of action. Maximum rate is 36 fl oz/acre/season.
medications.research_source: University of Minnesota Extension — Corn Gray Leaf Spot / UGA Extension Pest Management Handbook
medications.severity_threshold: Apply when GLS lesions are present on or above the ear leaf at tasseling on susceptible hybrids in high-risk fields

medications.timing: Apply at VT–R1. Three-way premix offers broad-spectrum control and extended residual activity.
medications.notes: Do not apply within 30 days of harvest for forage, grain, or stover. Higher cost; most justified on high-yield-potential fields with susceptible hybrids and confirmed GLS.
medications.research_source: Crop Protection Network — Fungicide Efficacy for Control of Corn Foliar Diseases / EPA product label
medications.severity_threshold: Same as single-mode products; preferred for heavy pressure or when extended residual activity is needed

blight.description: Northern corn leaf blight (Exserohilum turcicum) produces long, elliptical, cigar-shaped tan to gray-green lesions 1–6 inches long. Spreads rapidly under cool, wet weather.
cultural_controls: Plant resistant hybrids — look for hybrids with Ht1, Ht2, Htm1, or quantitative resistance
Rotate away from corn to reduce infected residue on the soil surface
Encourage residue breakdown with tillage or in-field composting
Scout from V12 through silking; infection before tasseling causes greatest yield loss

medications.timing: Apply at or before tasseling when lesions are present on the third leaf below the ear or higher on susceptible hybrids.
medications.notes: Maximum seasonal rate is 16 fl oz/acre (up to 4 applications at 4 fl oz). Triazoles provide curative as well as protective activity; good resistance management choice when alternated with strobilurins.
medications.research_source: University of Minnesota Extension — Northern Corn Leaf Blight / UGA Extension Pest Management Handbook
medications.severity_threshold: Economic threshold: lesions present on the ear leaf or above at tasseling on a susceptible hybrid

medications.timing: Apply at VT–R1. Premix offers improved control over single-mode products for high-pressure situations.
medications.notes: Do not apply within 30 days of harvest for field corn/popcorn forage, grain, or stover. Do not use an adjuvant with this product in corn. Maximum 2 applications per season.
medications.research_source: Crop Protection Network — Fungicide Efficacy for Control of Corn Foliar Diseases / EPA product label
medications.severity_threshold: Same as single-mode; preferred when both NCLB and gray leaf spot pressure are present

Black Rot Grape Vine.description: Black rot (Guignardia bidwellii) causes circular tan lesions with dark borders on leaves, and mummifies berries into hard, black, shrivelled fruit. Spreads rapidly during wet periods from bud break through fruit set.
cultural_controls: Remove all mummified fruit from the vine and the vineyard floor before bud break
Prune out infected wood and destroy prunings — do not leave them in the vineyard
Prune to open the canopy and promote rapid drying after rain
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip irrigation where possible
Scout from bud break through veraison; the period from 2 weeks before bloom to 4 weeks after is most critical

medications.trade_name: Mancozeb (various brands, e.g. Dithane, Manzate Pro-Stick, Penncozeb)
medications.water_volume: 25–200 gal/acre (lower volumes acceptable early season when canopy is small; 100+ gal/acre later in the season)
medications.timing: Begin applications at bud break (0.5-inch shoot) and continue on a 7–10 day schedule pre-bloom, 10–14 days post-bloom, through the critical infection period (bloom through 4 weeks post-bloom). Protective only; apply before rain events.
medications.notes: Strictly a protectant — must be applied before infection. Maximum seasonal use across all mancozeb-containing products is 18–19.2 lb active ingredient/acre (roughly 24 lb product/acre at typical formulations), reached at about 6 applications at the maximum rate. Cannot legally be applied within 66 days of harvest under any circumstance.
medications.research_source: Penn State Extension — Black Rot of Grape / Ohio State University Extension / Double A Vineyards Extension summary
medications.severity_threshold: Preventive program; begin at bud break regardless of initial disease presence in high-risk vineyards

medications.timing: Apply at 10–21 day intervals for powdery mildew/black rot, or 10–14 days for downy mildew, beginning at early shoot growth. Provides both protective and curative activity. Most critical window: 2 weeks before bloom through 4 weeks after bloom.
medications.notes: Do not make more than 2 sequential applications before rotating to a different mode of action. Maximum 28 fl oz/acre/season (4 applications at the 7 fl oz rate). Do NOT apply to Concord, Concord Seedless, or Thomcord grapes — phytotoxicity risk; use caution on other native/hybrid varieties.
medications.research_source: Penn State Extension — Grape Fungicide Programs / Michigan State University Extension / EPA product label
medications.severity_threshold: Use in rotation with mancozeb or captan during the high-risk bloom period

Blight Grape Vine.description: Grape downy mildew (Plasmopara viticola) produces oily, angular yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with white downy sporulation beneath. Infected shoots, tendrils, and clusters can be stunted or killed in severe outbreaks.
cultural_controls: Remove infected shoots and leaves during dry weather to reduce sporulation
Sanitise pruning tools between plants with 70% isopropyl alcohol
Improve canopy ventilation through shoot positioning, leaf removal, and hedging
Avoid overhead irrigation and minimise leaf wetness duration
Scout after rain events in warm weather (>50°F / 10°C); primary infection period is late spring to early summer

medications.timing: Apply at early shoot growth (2–4 inch shoots) and again at early bloom only if downy mildew is actually observed. Systemic (mefenoxam) component provides curative activity; protectant (mancozeb) component provides contact protection.
medications.notes: Do not exceed 2 applications per season. Mefenoxam/Ridomil is extremely prone to resistance development — many extension specialists recommend limiting this product to just 1 application per season even where the label permits 2, and only when downy mildew is actively present.
medications.research_source: Penn State Extension — Downy Mildew of Grape / Cornell Fruit Resources / Ohio Grape-Wine Extension Newsletter
medications.severity_threshold: Apply at first detection of oily spots on leaves or when 10 consecutive hours of leaf wetness occur at temperatures above 50°F following bud break

medications.dosage_rate: 6 fl oz/acre (confirm exact rate against the current state-specific supplemental label, as rates have varied by formulation/region)
medications.timing: Apply preventatively, before infection, on a 7–10 day schedule during periods of high downy mildew risk. Always tank-mix with a contact fungicide from a different FRAC group (e.g., mancozeb or captan); this product is not labeled for use alone.
medications.notes: Do not make more than 1 application before rotating to a fungicide with a different mode of action. Maximum 5 applications per year. The 28-day PHI is significantly longer than older guidance suggested — do not apply within 28 days of intended harvest.
medications.research_source: Michigan State University Extension — Newer Fungicide Chemistries for Grapes / University of Maryland Extension Fungicide Spray Guidelines
medications.severity_threshold: Use when downy mildew risk is high based on weather-based disease models or observed sporangia
